A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Agentic Reasoning, with matching core components, examples, and retained results. The text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. v1 ends with references and has no separate appendix; v2's Section 7 appendix was included in the assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPQA evaluations, expert-assessed deep-research pass rates, tool-use analyses, and a Werewolf experiment.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, human ratings, tool and memory ablations, and efficiency comparisons, including additional experiments in the appendix.

M1.justification: The three-agent architecture remains, but the Web-Search procedure is substantially revised. v1 Section 2.4 describes contextual summarization of retrieved pages; v2 Section 2.3 introduces query breakdown, relevance reranking, threshold-triggered query refinement, and RAG. Section 3.4.2 explicitly selects this combination and excludes separate Knowledge Refinement from the final design.

E1.justification: v2 adds Humanity's Last Exam, GAIA, and FreshWiki, extending evaluation to broader expert subjects, general assistant tasks requiring browsing and tools, and Wikipedia-style article generation. GPQA, professional research questions in finance/medicine/law, and the Werewolf and reasoning examples remain.

E2.justification: The GPQA comparator set changes: several Qwen2.5 and plain-RAG rows disappear, while DeepSeek-R1 and o3-mini baselines appear and o1 replaces o1-preview. The professional deep-research comparison expands beyond Gemini to DirectGen, RAG, RAgent, Search-O1, and STORM. Appendix comparisons additionally evaluate Read-agent, MemoryBank, MemGPT, Perplexity Deep Research, GPT Deep Research, and direct API calling.

E3.justification: Professional research evaluation changes from expert pass/fail rates to four 1-5 ratings. New experiments introduce ROUGE/entity-recall evaluation, latency measurements, memory/API controls, and GPQA analysis grouped by reasoning length and tool calls. The GPQA Extended comparison is removed. The newly stated total of 56 research questions is a disclosure, not evidence that the original sample increased.

E4.justification: v2 adds toolbox and tool-combination ablations, search-component ablations, and Mind-Map comparisons across reasoning lengths. The appendix adds alternative-memory, efficiency, and agent-versus-API analyses. Werewolf gains a without-Mind-Map control. The earlier standalone analysis advocating tool-count-based test-time selection is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports statistical uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, seeds, or statistical replication counts. The plots and tables continue to present point estimates. v2's discussion of agents expressing confidence concerns model behavior, not uncertainty estimation for experimental results.

E6.justification: v2 adds HLE accuracy of 23.8%, GAIA average accuracy of 66.13%, FreshWiki scores, human ratings, and numerous ablation and timing results. Original GPQA values 88.1/58.3/79.6 are retained and labeled QwQ-based; the new 94.5/73.7/80.5 values use DeepSeek-R1 and are not a same-configuration improvement. GPQA Extended results disappear. Werewolf's 72% win rate remains, with a newly reported 36% without Mind-Map.

T1.justification: v1 Section 2.1 defines the task mapping and a joint autoregressive probability factorization for reasoning and answer generation. This formal preliminary section is removed from v2 and is not relocated to its appendix. Neither version contains substantive theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 broadly claims superiority over existing models and emphasizes test-time scalability and potential verifier/reward-model use. v2 instead emphasizes SOTA among public models, comparability to OpenAI Deep Research, and a superior Web-Search design supported by ablations. The verifier/reward-model contribution is dropped from the main claims, with test-time computing relegated to future work.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning tool synergy, redundancy between Knowledge Refinement and reranking, and Mind-Map's prevention of reasoning drift and repeated mistakes. Its new limitations section expands earlier warnings about tool inaccuracies to computational overhead, sequential latency, missing source-credibility verification, and hallucination propagation. The appendix adds an explanation based on communicating uncertain agent outputs.

D1.justification: v2 Section 3.1 newly specifies reasoning and agent models, generation parameters, Bing retrieval depth, Cohere reranking thresholds and iteration limits, Python version, and default pass1 reporting. The appendix supplies the human-rating rubric, and the research-question total is disclosed. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the code repository link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated Related Work section positioning the framework against AutoGPT, LangChain, hierarchical planning, and task-specific agents. It expands the claimed research gap to agent integration, delegation, and tool synergy. New benchmark, retrieval, clustering, and memory-system references further broaden the positioning beyond v1's introductory discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten, and the introduction gains an explicit contribution list. The preliminary formalism and Main Findings section disappear; their surrounding narrative is reorganized into expanded experimental analyses. New implementation, related-work, limitations, and appendix sections substantially change the document structure. The title and author block also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds a front-page HLE table and numerous benchmark, rating, ablation, and efficiency tables. The GPQA table gains an overall column and revised structure. New toolbox and Mind-Map bar charts replace the earlier tool-call/pass-rate presentation. The workflow, medical, and riddle illustrations are largely retained, while the Werewolf display is reduced from two graphs to one.

improvement.justification: v1 provides little direct testing of its tool-selection and memory explanations and sparse implementation information. v2 substantially addresses these deficiencies through component ablations, alternative-memory and API controls, explicit implementation settings, and a documented human-rating rubric. Its limitations discussion also improves qualification of the claims. Reporting weaknesses remain: uncertainty is still absent, and Section 7.2.2 incorrectly claims faster performance than Perplexity despite Table 8 showing 6.8 versus 3.1 minutes. These issues limit confidence but do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidential support and reproducibility information.
